reply.text:
Let me look at what your bench has actually been doing. I can't see any bench logged yet, so I can't tell you where it stalled or for how long. If you've been benching outside the app, give me your recent top sets, like 185×5 for the last few weeks, and I'll read it properly.

In general, a stalled bench usually comes down to one of a few things:

- **Volume:** most people stall because they're doing too little, not too much. Hitting bench twice a week, with 3 to 5 hard sets each session, often gets things moving again.
- **Rep ranges:** swap your usual 5s for a few weeks of 8 to 10, or the reverse. Changing the stimulus beats grinding the same numbers.
- **Small jumps:** move up by the smallest plates you have, and stop each set with 1 or 2 reps in reserve rather than grinding to failure every time.
- **Pauses:** a one-second pause on the chest cleans up your technique and builds strength off the bottom.
- **Support work:** triceps and upper back (rows, dips, close-grip work) often decide whether a bench moves.
- **Recovery:** sleep and eating enough protein and food overall matter more than most people want to admit.

If you want, I can build a bench-focused block or add more pressing volume to your program. Tell me which and I'll set it up.
